name: pedestal
use: A rendered world with the product standing on a pedestal in the lower half and the claim written across the sky above it. The Norse claymation shape. Best when the pattern interrupt IS the ad — an unusual made world that stops the scroll before a word is read.

safe.why: Meta crops 9x16 to 4x5 in feed. Every line of type and the product sit inside this window so one asset covers every placement.

layout._measured_from: The swipe's own teardown: type strictly in the upper 45%, product pedestal 45-90% top and 25-75% wide, centre axis, unequal gaps grouping the type as one unit, the punch word angled ~5 degrees.
layout._product_note: The product is MORPHED INTO THE WORLD'S MATERIAL, not composited photoreal. Made by handing the real cutout to the edit model and asking for the same object sculpted in clay — which keeps the label exact while matching the set. Compositing the storefront photo into a clay diorama was the mismatch, 2026-09-02.
layout._adaptive_note: headline and punch follow the picture: they are laid into the quietest band the plate actually has, not a fixed percentage. The type sits where there is nothing to read over.
